newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil workers break off contract talks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil workers break off contract talks.

text.p: Colombia's main oil workers' union broke off collective contract negotiations with the state-run oil company Ecopetrol late Thursday in protest at a heavy jail sentence given to a union official, a union spokesman said.

The suspension of the talks followed news that Pedro Chaparro, former sectional head of the USO union at a refinery in the oil production center of Barrancabermeja, had been jailed for seven years on charges of rebellion.
Chaparro was first arrested four years ago but cleared of all charges by a regional judge before being retried by a national court in Bogota.

At least another 10 USO members were arrested in December on charges of dynamiting key oil installations and backing the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla group which specializes in attacks on the nation's oil infrastructure.
The jailing of Chaparro has firmed the union's resolve to take a leading role in the nationwide strike of state workers which is scheduled to begin on Feb. 11.

"With or without the jailing of Pedro we would take part in next Tuesday's strike. This sentence just gives us further strong political reasons for participating to the full," said Gustavo Triana, USO social services' secretary.

Other state unions also broke off their talks with government ministers earlier in the day as justice officials reopened a four-year-old investigations into 14 workers of the state telephone company Telecom. The men were charged with an illegal shutdown of Telecom facilities during a strike in 1993 but no action had been pursued until now.

The unions consider the legal action a provocative act by the government at a delicate stage in talks to avert next Tuesday's strike, which has been called in protest at below-inflation wage hikes for public sector employees and to oppose tougher anti-union legislation.

Hopes of a negotiated solution to avert the strike, which could lead to the total paralysis of the oil, health, telecommunications, education and public administration sectors, now seem to have faded.
"The unions' commitment to this strike is strong. I am pretty sure it will go ahead as planned," said Triana. -- Karl Penhaul, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
